correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier spectral decomposition gives a finite-time Cesàro interference sum. Half-flux degeneracies pair \(k\) with \(n-1-k\), yielding the exact stationary matrix and permanent antipodal cancellation. The sine-product formula yields a nonzero detuning spectral-gap lower bound, proving the all-entry \(1/(T|\delta|)\) estimate; the Duhamel norm estimate and dark channel prove the matching inverse-detuning lower threshold. Explicit surviving pair terms give the sinc crossover. Standard-library checker compares spectral integration with independent quadrature and tests boundary algebra; finite checks are not used to prove infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The qualitative simple-spectrum uniform Cesàro limit is explicitly known (Levine et al., Section 5, Theorem 5) and is credited. Inspected primary papers do not establish the explicit half-flux inverse-detuning cutoff with matching lower and upper bounds or the critical antipodal sinc crossover. Nonnegative real-weight and unweighted no-go results do not imply it. Originality remains provisional because a generic near-degeneracy dephasing theorem might cover the quantitative statement.
residual_risks: A general near-degenerate quantum time-average theorem could imply the same sinc crossover after specializing to flux cycles.
Search indexing may miss a paper using Aharonov-Bohm half-flux language or different notions of time averaging.
No external independent mathematical assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: The critical half-flux condition comes from physical destructive interference on a natural finite ring. The abrupt long-time change and its sharp inverse-detuning finite-time bottleneck, accompanied by an explicit universal sinc transition profile, quantify a motivated design/timing phenomenon not supplied by qualitative chiral circulant mixing theorems. The invariants are not chosen as arbitrary parameters; optimal prefactors and broader applications are not asserted.
